description: qDRIFT-style randomized product formula for Hamiltonian time evolution. Samples Hamiltonian terms according to term weights and applies a randomized sequence of single-term exponentials.
applicable_hamiltonians: Hamiltonians decomposable into a list of Hermitian matrix terms
Hamiltonians where randomized product formulas are useful as a depth or sampling tradeoff
Exploratory simulations comparing deterministic and randomized evolution
limitations: Individual trajectory results are stochastic unless a seed or sampled sequence is fixed
Requires enough samples for convergence of observables or state evolution
Legacy matrix-term inputs produce dense outputs only
Canonical Pauli inputs expose framework-neutral operations and reference circuits; hardware routing remains backend-specific
The standard bound applies to the expected quantum channel, not to every individual sampled trajectory

samples.description: Number of qDRIFT samples in the randomized product formula.

steps.description: Alias for samples, accepted for compatibility with other product-formula methods.

seed.description: Random seed for reproducible term sampling.

sampled_sequence.description: Optional archived term-index sequence to replay a qDRIFT trajectory exactly. Its length must equal samples.

term_weights.description: Legacy dense-input sampling weights. Canonical PauliHamiltonian inputs always use absolute Pauli coefficients and cannot be overridden.

execution.returns: EvolutionResult containing a sampled dense unitary, framework-neutral operation sequence, or compiled reference circuit plus seed, complete sampled sequence, logical and compiled costs, and provenance; run_ensemble(...) returns the expected dense validation channel.

complexity.gate_count: Exactly N sampled Pauli-term exponentials before reference-gate synthesis, where N is the sample count
complexity.circuit_depth: Backend-, connectivity-, and sampled-sequence-dependent; OpenQEvo reports depth after compilation to its fixed logical reference basis
complexity.error_scaling: The expected-channel diamond-distance bound is approximately 2(lambda * t)^2/N in the small-step regime, with a rigorous exponential correction; individual trajectory variation must be estimated separately

references.title: A random compiler for fast Hamiltonian simulation
